'''Wiesław Tadeusz Żelazko''' (16 February 1933 – 6 November 2025) was a Polish mathematician who specialised in [[functional analysis]] and the theory of topological and [[Banach algebra|Banach algebras]]. His name is attached to well-known theorems in [[Banach algebra|Banach algebra theory]], he held a full professorship at the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences]], received major national and scientific awards, and served as president of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]].<ref name=NaukaPL>{{cite web |title=Prof. zw. dr hab. Wiesław Tadeusz Żelazko |url=https://archiwum.nauka-polska.pl/#/profile/scientist?id=47312 |publisher=OPI PIB – Nauka Polska |access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Żelazko was born in [[Łódź]], Poland on 16 February 1933.<ref name="WTZ_PAI">{{Cite book |last=Żelazko |first=Wiesław Tadeusz |date=2001 |title='Kto jest kim w Polsce |journal= |publisher=PAI |pages=1103.}}</ref> He was a finalist in the second Polish Mathematical Olympiad in 1951. He studied mathematics at the [[University of Warsaw]], graduating in 1955 under the supervision of [[Roman Sikorski]]. He joined the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences]] (IMPAN) soon afterwards and completed his Ph.D. there in 1960 under [[Stanisław Mazur]] with a dissertation on locally bounded and m-convex rings.<ref name=PhDGen>{{cite web|access-date=19 December 2020 |language=en |title=Wiesław Żelazko in Mathematical Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=86239}}<!-- auto-translated from Polish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

== Academic career ==
Żelazko spent his entire professional career at IMPAN, where he became ''docent'' in 1965, ''extraordinary professor'' in 1971, and ''full professor'' in 1976.<ref name=ProfRP>{{cite web |title=Postanowienie Prezydenta RP o nadaniu orderów |url=https://isap.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/DocDetails.xsp?id=WMP20100280325 |date=2010 |access-date=13 November 2024}}</ref> His research focused on the structure theory of topological algebras, automatic continuity, and spectral properties of Banach algebras.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Żelazko |first=Wiesław |date=13 November 2025 |title=MathSciNet |url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/MRAuthorID/186870 |access-date=13 November 2025 |website=mathscinet.ams.org}}</ref> 

He supervised several doctoral students, including Zbigniew Słodkowski and Jaroslav Zemánek, both of whom later became prominent researchers in operator theory and Banach algebras.<ref name="PhDGen" />

== Personal life and death ==
Żelazko was married to Jowita Koncewicz.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Wasielewska |first=K. |date=2020 |title='Cyfrodziewczyny. Pionierki polskiej informatyki |journal= |publisher=Wydawnictwo Krytyki Politycznej |pages= |doi= |issn=}}</ref> He died on 6 November 2025, at the age of 92.<ref name=PTMzm>{{cite web |title=Zmarł Wiesław Żelazko (1933–2025) |url=https://www.ptm.org.pl/zawartosc/zmar%C5%82-wies%C5%82aw-%C5%BCelazko-1933-2025 |publisher=Polish Mathematical Society |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref>

=== Legacy ===
A short note that several theorems bear his name and that his results remain standard references.
Several theorems in functional analysis bear his name. The '''Gleason–Kahane–Żelazko theorem''', independently obtained by three authors, provides a geometric characterization of multiplicative linear functionals and has since become a standard result in Banach algebra theory. The '''Hirschfeld–Żelazko theorem''' offers another spectral criterion that found broad use in automatic continuity problems.

== Professional service ==
Żelazko was a member of the [[Warsaw Scientific Society]] and of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences|Mathematics Committee of the Polish Academy of Sciences]]. From 1983 to 1985, he served as president of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prezesi PTM |url=https://100latptm.matinf.uj.edu.pl/PTM-prezesi.php |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=100latptm.matinf.uj.edu.pl}}</ref>.

== Awards and honours ==
Żelazko received the '''Stefan Banach Prize''' (1967)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wiesław Żelazko {{!}} Polskie Towarzystwo Matematyczne |url=https://www.ptm.org.pl/laureaci/wieslaw-zelazko |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207034737/https://www.ptm.org.pl/laureaci/wieslaw-zelazko |archive-date=7 December 2023 |access-date=13 November 2025 |website=www.ptm.org.pl |language=pl}}</ref> and the '''Stefan Banach Medal''' (2000). He was also decorated with the [[Order of Polonia Restituta|Knight's Cross of Polonia Restituta]] (1979), [[Order of Polonia Restituta|Officer's Cross]] (1988), and [[Order of Polonia Restituta|Commander's Cross]] (2009) of the '''[[Order of Polonia Restituta]]''' for his contributions to Polish science.

== Selected publications ==
* Żelazko, W. ''Locally bounded and m-convex rings'' (doctoral thesis), IMPAN, 1960.
* Jarosz, K.; Żelazko, W. ''Topological algebras and Banach algebras''. In: ''Banach Center Publications'', vol. 67 (2005), 9–20.
